question: Sapna invested ₹20,300 on simple interest, partly at 10% per annum and partly at 4% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 4 years, then find the sum invested at 10% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Simple Interest is equal for two investments made for the same duration, the ratio of their principals is inversely proportional to their respective interest rates.

P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 4 : 10 = 2 : 5

Total ratio parts = 2 + 5 = 7

Sum invested at 10% (P₁) = (2 ÷ 7) × 20300 = ₹5800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total sum invested = ₹20,300

Rate for Part 1 (R₁) = 10% per annum, Time = 4 years

Rate for Part 2 (R₂) = 4% per annum, Time = 4 years

Interest from Part 1 = Interest from Part 2
